text:
Anya (PM): PRD draft for Dedicated Capacity (v0.9) posted: https://redwood.internal/prd/dedicated/v0.9. Asking product + eng + sres for quick alignment on: SLA targets, throughput sizing assumptions, autoscale acceptance criteria, and the fallback model behavior. Please drop short bullets.

Leo (Eng): reading now. quick Q — what request profile should we size to? avg tokens, %chat vs completion, and spike expectations?

Anya (PM): good call. baseline customers: 3 mid-market apps (sustained 50–200 rps), 2 enterprise pilots (sustained 1k rps with 5k rps bursts). Avg token per request: 18 (chat-like) for mid-market, 40 for enterprise. Target we agreed to size for: sustained 500 rps with 8k rps 30s bursts.

Marta (SRE): suggested SLA defaults for PRD: availability 99.95% monthly for Dedicated endpoints; error budget = 43.2m/month. Latency SLOs (examples): P95 <= 350ms for short-gen (<=64 tokens), P99 <= 1.2s. Also include a degraded SLA tier that auto-falls back to cheaper model variant on capacity pressure. Runbook + alerting required for >50% error budget burn in 24h.

Ryan (Product Ops): confirm: the degraded SLA == automatic fallback to quantized model variant with up to 2x latency increase but 40% cost reduction? we should call that out in acceptance criteria.

Anya (PM): yes — fallback behavior: prefer model variant that is architecture-compatible (same family); fallbacks must not change API shape. Documented in PRD under "Fallback rules". Ryan — add the pricing/contract language for degraded SLA.

Leo (Eng): quick sizing sketch: assumptions: avg tokens = 20, model perf ~15k tokens/s per A100-like GPU. For 500 rps -> 500 * 20 = 10k tokens/s. That maps to ~0.7 GPUs. With 30% headroom + batching inefficiency + KV cache cold start, recommend 2 GPUs baseline. For 8k rps burst: 8000 * 20 = 160k tokens/s -> ~11 GPUs; with 20% headroom -> 14 GPUs. So baseline pool 2, burst capacity up to 14. These numbers will vary with model/quantization.

Marta (SRE): autoscale rules we should validate in PRD:
- scale up trigger: queue depth > 200 requests for 5s OR GPU util > 70% for 60s
- scale down: GPU util < 30% for 120s and queue depth < 50 for 180s
- min_size = 1 GPU, desired = baseline (from sizing), max_size = baseline * 8 (cap burst)
- cooldowns: 60s for up, 180s for down.

Leo (Eng): adding edge cases to call out in acceptance criteria: cold KV cache increases per-token cost + latency for first N requests after a scale event; batch size variability under low qps; partial host failures (degrade to fallback variant must happen automatically within 90s).

Anya (PM): acceptance criteria draft (please thumbs up / edit):
- PRD defines SLA numbers and degraded tier behavior (owner: Anya)
- Baseline sizing calculations with explicit model perf assumptions (owner: Leo)
- Autoscale policy in config and validated e2e with canary traffic (owner: Marta)
- Fallback model variants defined and verified for API parity (owner: Leo)
- Runbook for error budget burn and failover steps (owner: Marta)
- Customer-facing docs and contract language for degraded SLA (owner: Ryan)

Marta (SRE): +1 to those. Also add acceptance test: simulated burst test that verifies 90th percentile failover time < 2min and no more than 5% request loss.

Ryan (Product Ops): I'll draft degraded SLA contract paragraph and sample commit tiers (small/medium/large) with corresponding baseline GPUs and burst caps. Aim to have a draft by Thu EOD.

Leo (Eng): will add per-model perf table and update GPU throughput numbers. Ask: do we want to also include a "warm pool" option for pilots to reduce cold-starts? that would change cost math.

Anya (PM): yes include warm pool as optional add-on. note in PRD as tradeoff (cost vs latency).

Marta (SRE): small autoscale example for the PRD (paste into PRD ops section):
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_gpus: 1
  baseline_gpus: 2
  max_gpus: 16
  scale_up:
    - condition: queue_depth > 200 for 5s
    - condition: gpu_util > 70% for 60s
  scale_down:
    - condition: gpu_util < 30% for 120s
    - condition: queue_depth < 50 for 180s
  cooldowns:
    up: 60s
    down: 180s
```

Anya (PM): perfect. next steps / owners: Leo updates sizing table (due Tue), Marta adds scale tests + runbook (due Wed), Ryan drafts contract wording (Thu), I'll consolidate and send PRD for final review Fri. Thanks all :thumbsup:
